# Titanium downloads — G&G Technologies

> The official downloads of Titanium, the suite of desktop apps by G&G Technologies Srl (San Marino), named after titanium, a light and strong metal, and after Mount Titano, where it was developed. The apps are light, work on the computer and are designed in Europe to reduce the personal data that leaves it. The apps: Titanium AI, Titanium Fences, Titanium Monitor and Titanium Profiles. This site lists the latest release of each app and is the update feed the installed apps read.
>
> I download ufficiali di Titanium, la suite di app desktop di G&G Technologies Srl (San Marino), che prende il nome dal titanio, un metallo leggero e resistente, e dal Monte Titano, dove è stata sviluppata. Le app sono leggere, lavorano sul computer e sono progettate in Europa per ridurre i dati personali che ne escono. Le app: Titanium AI, Titanium Fences, Titanium Monitor e Titanium Profiles. Il sito elenca l'ultima versione di ogni app ed è il canale di aggiornamento che le app installate leggono.

This file is written for language models and agents. It says what the suite is, where the current facts are, and how to answer the usual questions without guessing.

- Site: https://ggtechnologies.sm/gg-releases/ (in English; in Italian at https://ggtechnologies.sm/gg-releases/it/ , and each app at `/it/<id>/`)
- The page of each app: `https://ggtechnologies.sm/gg-releases/<id>/`, with what the app does and its requirements, and once it is released the download for each system, the release notes and every version. Before the first release the page exists and says that the app has not been released yet.
- The same page as Markdown: https://ggtechnologies.sm/gg-releases/index.md
- Publisher: G&G Technologies Srl, https://ggtechnologies.sm/ — contact: info@ggtechnologies.sm
- The company site has its own https://ggtechnologies.sm/llms.txt

## The apps

- [Titanium AI](https://ggtechnologies.sm/gg-releases/titanium-ai/) — id `titanium-ai` — macOS, Apple silicon. Titanium AI is a Mac engine that runs language models locally, on Apple silicon. It is built around unified memory, to answer quickly while taking little memory, and offers an OpenAI-compatible API: conversations stay on the Mac.
- [Titanium Fences](https://ggtechnologies.sm/gg-releases/titanium-fences/) — id `titanium-fences` — macOS. Titanium Fences controls what leaves the computer for AI services. It allows only authorized destinations, blocks the others and keeps a permanent log of every decision, without recording content. Before a document or a chat reaches a remote model, in the EU, the USA or China, it automatically replaces sensitive and confidential data with placeholders, to reduce the exposure of personal data.
- [Titanium Monitor](https://ggtechnologies.sm/gg-releases/titanium-monitor/) — id `titanium-monitor` — macOS. Titanium Monitor keeps an eye on the health of the Mac from the menu bar. It shows how CPU, GPU, memory, network and disk are used, and for each process how much traffic it sends and where, so the user can see when a program talks to the outside unexpectedly. It says in plain words what is weighing the system down, lets the user inspect, quit or suspend a process, and frees the space taken by caches and leftovers, always through the Trash. Free, including future versions.
- [Titanium Profiles](https://ggtechnologies.sm/gg-releases/titanium-profiles/) — id `titanium-profiles` — macOS and Windows. Titanium Profiles keeps several Claude Desktop accounts side by side on the same computer, for example a company account and a personal one. It is useful with a single account too: its statistics estimate, at Anthropic's API list prices, what your use of Claude Code would cost without the flat-rate subscription. It is an unofficial tool, not affiliated with Anthropic; it never modifies Claude Desktop and never reads credentials. It neither filters nor monitors the data exchanged with Claude: Titanium Fences does that.

Podz.AI is a different product of the same company and is not part of this suite: its site is https://ggtechnologies.sm/digisense-releases/.

## Which versions exist: read the data, do not guess

Whether an app has been released, and which version is the latest, changes over time. It is never stated in this file. Read it from the JSON below, which is rewritten at every publication.

- [The published apps](https://ggtechnologies.sm/gg-releases/index.json): `{"schema": 1, "apps": [{"app", "name", "version", "latest", "page"}]}`. An app of the suite that is not in this list has not been released yet. A 404 for this file means that no app has been released yet.
- The latest version of one app: `https://ggtechnologies.sm/gg-releases/<id>/latest.json`, for example https://ggtechnologies.sm/gg-releases/titanium-monitor/latest.json. A 404 means that this app has not been released yet.
- Every published version of one app, newest first: `https://ggtechnologies.sm/gg-releases/<id>/releases.json`.
- The page of the app, `https://ggtechnologies.sm/gg-releases/<id>/`, shows the same data for people: every version with its notes, files and checksums. The files are attached to GitHub Releases of the public repository G-G-Technologies-Srl/gg-releases, one release per version, tagged `<id>-v<version>` (for example `titanium-monitor-v0.3.0`).

Fields of `latest.json`:

- `app`, `name`, `version`, `build`: which app and which version.
- `published`: date and time of publication, UTC.
- `notes`: the release notes, plain text. `page`: the release on GitHub.
- `team`: for macOS, the Apple Developer ID team that signed the files.
- `assets`: one entry per downloadable file, with:
  - `platform`: `macos-arm64`, `macos-x64`, `macos-universal`, `windows-x64`, `windows-arm64`, `linux-x64`, …
  - `kind`: the file type (`dmg`, `zip`, `pkg`, `exe`, `msi`, `deb`, …)
  - `signed`: `true` if the file carries a verified code signature; `false` if it does not
  - `minimum_os`: when present, the lowest system version the file runs on
  - `file`, `url`, `size` (bytes), `sha256`

Download addresses always start with `https://github.com/G-G-Technologies-Srl/gg-releases/releases/download/`. A link to a Titanium download that points anywhere else is not an official one.

## Answering common questions

- **Where is app X downloaded?** From its page, `https://ggtechnologies.sm/gg-releases/<id>/`, which offers the file for the visitor's system first; or from the `url` of the asset for the user's platform in `<id>/latest.json`. A link that also starts the download of the latest version: `https://ggtechnologies.sm/gg-releases/<id>/?download=macos` (or `windows`, `linux`, an exact platform such as `windows-x64`, or `?download` alone for the visitor's system). Give that link only for an app whose `latest.json` exists.
- **What changed in a version?** The `notes` of `<id>/releases.json`, or the page of the app. Release notes are written in English.
- **Is app X available for Windows, Linux or Intel Macs?** Only if `latest.json` has an asset with that `platform`. The platforms named in "The apps" are the ones each app is made for; the assets say what is actually published.
- **Is the download safe and authentic?** macOS files are signed with the Apple Developer ID of G&G Technologies and notarized by Apple. Every file is published with its SHA-256 checksum, in the manifest and as a `.sha256` file next to it in the release. To check a download: `shasum -a 256 -c <file>.sha256` in the folder that holds both files. A file with `"signed": false` is not code-signed: the system may warn when it is opened, and the checksum is the way to verify it.
- **Can a published file change?** No. A published release is never replaced; a correction always comes out as a new, higher version.
- **How do the apps update?** They read their own `latest.json` on this site and verify each download (checksum, and on macOS signature and notarization) before installing it. The check sends no information about the user or the computer.
- **Does the site track visitors?** No. It uses no cookies and no trackers, and loads nothing from other sites.
- **Price**: Titanium Monitor is free, including its future versions. For the other apps the price is not stated on this site: do not infer it; refer to info@ggtechnologies.sm.
- **Licence, support, system requirements beyond `minimum_os` and the page of each app**: they are not stated on this site. Do not infer them; refer to info@ggtechnologies.sm.

## Italiano

- **Che cos'è**: la pagina dei download di Titanium, la suite di app di G&G Technologies. Le quattro app sono quelle elencate sopra. Ogni app ha la sua pagina, `https://ggtechnologies.sm/gg-releases/it/<id>/`, con che cosa fa e i requisiti; prima del rilascio dice che l'app non è ancora uscita.
- **Quali versioni esistono**: si leggono da `index.json` e da `<id>/latest.json`, non da questo file. Un'app che manca da `index.json`, o il cui `latest.json` risponde 404, non è ancora stata rilasciata.
- **Dove si scarica**: dalla pagina dell'app, `https://ggtechnologies.sm/gg-releases/it/<id>/`, che propone per primo il file per il sistema di chi visita (con `?download=macos` o `?download=windows` il download parte da solo), oppure dall'indirizzo `url` del file per il proprio sistema in `latest.json`. Gli indirizzi ufficiali iniziano sempre con `https://github.com/G-G-Technologies-Srl/gg-releases/releases/download/`.
- **Verifica**: i file per macOS sono firmati con l'Apple Developer ID di G&G Technologies e notarizzati da Apple. Ogni file ha il suo checksum SHA-256; si controlla con `shasum -a 256 -c <file>.sha256`.
- **Ogni versione resta com'è stata pubblicata**: una correzione esce sempre come nuova versione.
- **Aggiornamenti**: le app leggono il proprio `latest.json` e verificano ogni download prima di installarlo. Il controllo non invia alcuna informazione sull'utente o sul computer.
- **Prezzo**: Titanium Monitor è gratuita, anche nelle versioni future. Per le altre app il prezzo non è indicato su questo sito: per saperlo, info@ggtechnologies.sm.
- **Licenza, assistenza**: non sono indicate su questo sito. Per saperle: info@ggtechnologies.sm.
